threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver shouts 'next stop’ after a 30-second wait. We’re all used to just standing there.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele. Kind of magical, until the person next to me dropped their kebab.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? When I saw a street vendor juggling flaming kebabs at a corner near Tempelhofer Feld, and no one batted an eye.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do I see spontaneous dance parties break out in U-Bahn stations during strikes. It's like the city's heartbeat, refusing to stop even when transport does.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they avoid eye contact with tourists at the taco truck but still know the secret menu by heart.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni light rail today, and someone brought a dog that wouldn't stop barking. Classic SF moment—only in this city can a bark become a symphony.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the parks are for picnics, but locals know they’re just for people-watching while sipping café amb llet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the ticket machines—still fumbling with the language settings and staring blankly at the options.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 243 bus is a reliable way to get around. Locals know it’s just a suggestion, not a schedule.
Caught a night bus from Brixton, saw a guy serenading a cat on the seat. The driver just shook his head, but the cat seemed to enjoy it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy selling homemade falafel from a stand on the corner while debating the latest BVG strike with his customers. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop open 24/7, where the line is always long, even at 4 AM. It's the pulse of the night here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local when they know which taco truck has the best al pastor after a late night out—hint: it’s not the one on 24th.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw someone feeding a pigeon in Civic Center while waiting for the bus. Muni was late again, but the bird seemed unfazed. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but locals know it’s the vibrant plazas and quirky boutiques that make it home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still take photos of every building with a colorful door, like it's a rare sight. Locals just walk right past them.
